title: Purity of the geometric coinvariants
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and a field isomorphism $\iota:\Omega\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse $\Omega$-Weil sheaf in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w\in\mathbf R$ [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Put $\mathcal F^\vee=\mathcal Hom_\Omega(\mathcal F,\Omega_X)$ with its contragredient Weil structure, and define the geometric coinvariants by
$$W=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee,\qquad F_W=(T^{-1})^*,$$
where $T$ is geometric Frobenius on $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\vee)$ [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] and the final dual is the ordinary $\Omega$-linear dual. Then $W$ is finite-dimensional and $(W,F_W)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], allowing $W=0$. When $X$ is connected and $V$ is the geometric fundamental representation [def-wf-fundamental-representation], there are natural identifications
$$\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\vee)=(V^\vee)^{\pi_1(X)}=(V_{\pi_1(X)})^\vee,$$
so $W=V_{\pi_1(X)}$ with its induced Frobenius, the maximal geometrically constant quotient. Here invariants, coinvariants and the contragredient action have the meanings of [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. For general $X$, global sections are the product over its finitely many connected components, with Frobenius allowed to permute them.

proof.text: Apply [lem-tw-dual-negation] to $\mathcal F$ on the finite-type scheme $X_0$. Thus $\mathcal G=\mathcal F^\vee$ is lisse with the contragredient Weil structure and is punctually pure of weight $-w$. Apply [lem-a1-lisse-sections-stalk-evaluation] to $\mathcal G$: $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$ is finite-dimensional, its geometric Frobenius $T$ is invertible, and evaluation into finitely many closed-point stalks is injective. These statements apply without connectedness or smoothness; the separated finite-type and coefficient hypotheses are precisely those in force.

source.place: Second paragraph, closed-point eigenvalue argument; generalized dual-section formulation, with the comparison and finiteness isolated explicitly

proof.text: Let $\beta$ be any eigenvalue of $T$ and choose $a\ne0$ with $Ta=\beta a$. Finite stalk detection [lem-a1-lisse-sections-stalk-evaluation] gives a closed point $y_i$ at which $b=\operatorname{ev}_{\bar y_i}(a)\ne0$. Write $d=[\kappa(y_i):k_0]\ge1$. Repeated application of $Ta=\beta a$ gives $T^d a=\beta^d a$, and the evaluation identity in that same lemma gives $F_{y_i}b=\beta^d b$. Hence $\beta^d$ is a local Frobenius eigenvalue of $\mathcal G$. Its punctual purity from step 1 and [def-weil-punctual-weights] give $|\iota(\beta)|^d=(q^d)^{-w/2}=(q^{-w/2})^d$. Both sides are powers of nonnegative real numbers and $d>0$, so injectivity of the positive integer power on nonnegative reals yields $|\iota(\beta)|=q^{-w/2}$. Thus $(A,T)$ is pure of weight $-w$ in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].

source.place: Second paragraph, closed-point eigenvalue argument; generalized dual-section formulation, with the comparison and finiteness isolated explicitly

proof.text: By definition $W=A^\vee$ and $F_W=(T^{-1})^*$. Since $A$ is finite-dimensional and $T$ invertible, the dual-spectrum formula of [p-linear-spectra] says that each eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $F_W$ is $\beta^{-1}$ for an eigenvalue $\beta\ne0$ of $T$. Step 2 gives $|\iota(\lambda)|=|\iota(\beta)|^{-1}=q^{w/2}$. This is purity of weight $w$ in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. The linear dual of a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional, and the zero space has no eigenvalues, so the statement includes $W=0$.

source.place: Second paragraph, closed-point eigenvalue argument; generalized dual-section formulation, with the comparison and finiteness isolated explicitly

proof.text: For the connected-case description, the exact tensor fibre equivalence in [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) identifies the dual sheaf with the dual representation. A global section is the same as a morphism from the unit sheaf (send $1$ to that section, and on each object send $c$ to $c$ times its restriction); full faithfulness identifies these maps with equivariant maps $\Omega\to V^\vee$. Such a map is determined by its value at $1$, which must lie in $(V^\vee)^{\pi_1(X)}$. With the dual action in [def-real-weil-representation-operations], a functional is invariant exactly when it kills every $gv-v$, so it factors uniquely through $V_{\pi_1(X)}$. This gives the two displayed identifications. The Frobenius compatibility follows by naturality with respect to the Weil isomorphism and its degree-one action from [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Dualizing gives $W\simeq V_{\pi_1(X)}$ with its induced Frobenius. Every map from $V$ to a representation on which $\pi_1(X)$ acts trivially kills $gv-v$, so factors uniquely through this quotient: it is maximal geometrically constant.

source.place: First paragraph, coinvariant quotient and Weil action; section-to-representation interpretation of the generalized statement

proof.text: The base change $X$ is of finite type over $k$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The locally finite family of irreducible components in [lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite] is finite here: choose neighbourhoods meeting finitely many components and take a finite subcover using quasi-compactness. Form the finite graph whose vertices are these irreducible components and whose edges mean nonempty intersection. The union belonging to each graph component is connected (each irreducible component is connected and successive unions meet); it is closed, as is its complement, both being finite unions of closed irreducible components. Thus these unions are the connected components of $X$ and form a finite disjoint open cover. Restrictions give $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\vee)\simeq\prod_C\Gamma(C,\mathcal F^\vee|_C)$: families glue uniquely because overlaps are empty. Frobenius acts through its permutation of these opens and the induced restriction maps. Steps 1–3 already allowed this permutation, since the evaluation identity used the degree of each chosen point separately.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$,
$X=X_0\otimes k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $X_0$
which is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Its *geometric
coinvariants* are $W:=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee$, the dual of the
global sections of the dual sheaf, with the Frobenius $F_W$ dual to the
one induced by the Weil structure. When $X$ is connected, with geometric
fundamental representation $V$ ([def-wf-fundamental-representation]),
$\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\vee)=(V^\vee)^{\pi_1(X)}=(V_{\pi_1(X)})^\vee$, so $W$
is the coinvariant quotient $V_{\pi_1(X)}$ — the maximal geometrically
constant quotient of $\mathcal F$ — with its induced Frobenius; in
general $\Gamma(X,-)$ is a product over the connected components of $X$.
Then $(W,F_W)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ (possibly $W=0$).

proof.text:
The geometric subgroup $\pi_1(U)$ of the Weil group of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation] is normal, so the subspace of $V$
spanned by the vectors $gv-v$, $g\in\pi_1(U)$, is stable under the Weil
group and $V\twoheadrightarrow W$ is a quotient Weil representation. On
$W$ the geometric subgroup acts trivially, so the action of any element
of degree one of the Weil group on $W$ is a single operator $F_W$,
independent of the chosen lift; an element of degree $d$ acts by
$F_W^d$.

Choose a closed point $x\in U_0$ (a maximal ideal of the coordinate
ring of a nonempty affine open; its residue field is finite over
$\mathbf F_q$) and put $d=[\kappa(x):\mathbf F_q]$. A local Frobenius
at $x$ is an element of degree $d$ of the Weil group, and under the
identification of $V$ with the stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ it acts as
the operator $F_x$ of [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Hence
$V\twoheadrightarrow W$ is an $F_x$-equivariant quotient onto
$(W,F_W^d)$. In a basis of $V$ extending a basis of the kernel, the
matrix of $F_x$ is block upper triangular ([p-linear-filtration]), so
every eigenvalue of $F_W^d$ is an eigenvalue of $F_x$ on
$\mathcal F_{\bar x}$, and has $\iota$-modulus
$|\kappa(x)|^{w/2}=q^{dw/2}$ by punctual purity
([def-weil-punctual-weights]). If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $F_W$,
then $\lambda^d$ is an eigenvalue of $F_W^d$, so
$|\iota(\lambda)|^d=q^{dw/2}$ and $|\iota(\lambda)|=q^{w/2}$. Thus
$(W,F_W)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ in the sense of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].
